es, background jobs & token KPIs on one page in the web GUI
# dsh-dashboard
> **Unofficial third-party plugin** — not affiliated with, sponsored, or endorsed by DeepSeek AI.
**Session Dashboard for DeepSeek Harness** — every session, task progress, waiting-for-approval stat
es, background jobs and token/KPI metrics on one page, injected straight into the harness web GUI. N
o separate server or page.
## Features
- **Sidebar trigger** — Dashboard toggle + sticky pin; icon-only rail mode with tooltips when the si

debar is collapsed
- **Full-screen panel** (never covers the sidebar):
- 18 KPI tiles, tone-coded (r
unning blue / completed green / waiting amber / errors red) — the status tiles double as clickable f

ilters
- Search + status filter chips with status dots (All / Running / Approval / Needs input / Err

ors / Completed / Idle)
- Session tables with labeled status pills, keyboard support (Enter opens, D

opens details), sticky column headers
- Attention ripple on sessions waiting for user approval/inpu

t
- Workspace grouping, live job activity feed, subagent hierarchy tree
- **Slide-over detail drawer
**: todo progress, live jobs, session stats, token-usage composition with legend, context-pressure g

auge
- **Floating live summary (sticky)** — follows you across pages, minimized pill with a waiting

counter
- **Notifications** — in-page toasts + audio chimes + native OS banners for completed / erro
r / waiting states, wired through a requestAnimationFrame frame bridge so they fire even when the ta

b is unfocused
- Status model splits approval / question / plan-review out of `pendingInteraction`;

errors come from crashed producer jobs
- Colors ride DSH design tokens (`--dsw-*`) — light/dark them
e for free; respects `prefers-reduced-motion`
## Requirements

- A running DeepSeek Harness install with the web GUI (this plugin only ships a client bundle)
- Nod
e.js >= 18 (only needed when building from source)

## Usage
| Action | How |
| Open the dashboard | **Dashboard** button in the sidebar footer (or the rail icon when collapsed)

|
| Pin the live summary | **Sticky** pin button |
| Open a session | single-click a row |
| Session

details | double-click a row, press **D**, or single-click in the sticky |
| Filter | click the KPI

tiles or the status chips |
| Close | **Esc** (closes the detail drawer first, then the panel) |
|
Toggle notifications | the bell in the panel header or sticky header (dot: green = banners granted,
ns | the bell in the panel header or sticky header (dot: green = banners granted, amber = blocked) |
### Notification sounds & banners
The first bell click warms the audio context, asks for window-notification permission and starts a k
eep-alive so background tabs never silence alerts.
If the bell dot stays amber:

1. Allow notifications for the harness origin in the browser (padlock icon in the address bar).
2. C
heck the OS-level setting for the browser app, e.g. Windows Settings -> System -> Notifications.
## How it works
The package registers one host-side plugin (an empty `apply`, purely to appear in the Loader) and on
e client bundle served at `/plugins/@jinhun-tqtteam/dsh-dashboard/client.js`. The bundle registers i
tself through `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` in the lazy-CJS shape the DSH client module system expe
cts, mounts three `shell.overlay` entries (panel, sticky, notifications) plus one `sidebar.footer.ac
tion` entry (the trigger), and receives the `openSession` descriptor through the standard `inject` m
ry (the trigger), and receives the `openSession` descriptor through the standard `inject` mechanism.

## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
| `bundle ... loaded without registering "<id>"` in the log | The loader entry `name` and the packag

e name differ — make them identical |
| Trigger button missing | The loader entry was not composed i

n yet — restart the harness after editing `cordis.patch.yml` |
| Panel opens but is empty | Sessions

appear once the host publishes them; make sure at least one session exists |
| No sound while the t
ab is unfocused | Toggle the bell once per page load (it enables the keep-alive + audio warm-up) |
